title: SQLite open, migrations, test db and tasks table
description:
Source of truth: docs/thoughts/2026-09-17-increment-01-task-basics.md → 'Under the hood → Persistence', 'Table tasks', 'Guards added', 'Documentation added'. Read it in full first.

Deliver src/lib/db/ using Node's built-in node:sqlite (DatabaseSync), no npm dependency:
- open.ts: `openDatabase(path: string): DatabaseSync` — creates the parent directory if missing (mkdirSync recursive), opens the file, runs `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` and `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, calls applyMigrations, returns the handle.
- migrate.ts: `type Migration = { version: number; name: string; sql: string }`, `MIGRATIONS: Migration[]` (imports migration0001), `applyMigrations(db: DatabaseSync, migrations: Migration[] = MIGRATIONS): number` (returns how many were applied). Creates `schema_migrations(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL)` if missing; applies each migration whose version is not yet recorded, ascending, each inside a transaction (BEGIN / COMMIT, ROLLBACK on error), inserting the row with `new Date().toISOString()`.
- migrations/0001_tasks.ts: `migration0001: Migration` with version 1, name "tasks", sql creating
  tasks(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(title) BETWEEN 1 AND 200), notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK (length(notes) <= 2000), done_at TEXT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL)
  and `CREATE INDEX tasks_open_idx ON tasks(done_at, created_at DESC)`.
- client.ts: `getDb(): DatabaseSync` — process-wide singleton (module-level variable, also stored on globalThis under a Symbol so Next.js dev hot reload reuses it), path from `readEnv().databasePath` (src/lib/env.ts already exists). Only server code may import it.
- test-db.ts: `createTestDb(): { db: DatabaseSync; path: string; close(): void }` — a migrated database at `join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "harness-demo-")), "test.db")`; close() closes the handle and removes the temp directory (rmSync recursive, force).
- index.ts re-exporting openDatabase, applyMigrations, MIGRATIONS, getDb, createTestDb and the Migration type.

Also deliver src/lib/tasks/types.ts (the contract wave 2 consumes; create it exactly):
  export type Task = { id: number; title: string; notes: string; doneAt: string | null; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string };
  export type TaskInput = { title: string; notes: string };

Guard test scripts/check-rules.test.ts (vitest, node project, already included by vitest.config.ts): walks src/ recursively and fails if any .ts/.tsx file other than src/lib/env.ts contains the text `process.env`, or any file outside src/lib/db/ imports "node:sqlite". Use readdirSync recursive; the test must pass on the current tree.

Test cases (test-first) in src/lib/db/open.integration.test.ts (node project; use createTestDb or a mkdtemp path):
- openDatabase on `<fresh tmpdir>/nested/dir/app.db` creates the file and the nested directory.
- after opening, `SELECT version, name FROM schema_migrations` returns [{version: 1, name: "tasks"}], and `PRAGMA table_info(tasks)` lists exactly id, title, notes, done_at, created_at, updated_at.
- opening the same path a second time returns a handle and applyMigrations reports 0 applied (assert via a second explicit applyMigrations call returning 0).
- applyMigrations with a custom list [{version: 7, name: "x", sql: "CREATE TABLE x(a)"}] on a fresh db applies it once and a second call returns 0.
- a migration whose sql fails leaves no schema_migrations row (transaction rolled back) and throws.
- createTestDb(): the file exists while open; after close() the temp directory no longer exists.
- inserting a task with a 201-character title throws (CHECK constraint).

Documentation (same commit, shape per docs/current/_documentation_principles.md; run `pnpm docs:check` — missing SVG renders are a warning for you, everything else must be clean):
- docs/current/how/persistence.md (tier 2): intro paragraph; `![Persistence](../diagrams/persistence.svg)` then `<!-- diagram: persistence -->` above a Mermaid flowchart showing openDatabase → ensure dir → PRAGMAs → applyMigrations (schema_migrations check → run pending in transaction) → handle, with getDb (app, env path) and createTestDb (tests, temp file, close removes) as the two callers; `## Key entry points` table with the exact paths and exports above; mechanism prose with exact values (WAL, foreign_keys, table names, ISO timestamps); failure modes table (e.g. "database is locked", missing directory, running e2e and dev against the same file).
- docs/current/data-model.md (tier 3): `<!-- diagram: data-model -->` Mermaid erDiagram of tasks and schema_migrations (as the lead diagram after the intro, referenced as ../diagrams/data-model.svg is NOT right for a top-level page: use `![Data model](diagrams/data-model.svg)`), then one table per table with column, type, constraint, meaning, the index, the ordering rules (open: created_at DESC, id DESC; done: done_at DESC, id DESC) and the migration ledger (0001 tasks).
- Add both pages to docs/current/_overview.md (Documents table, Diagrams table with ids `persistence` and `data-model`, and set the last-update line to today naming this tick) and to docs/current/README.md's document map. Update setup.md's sentence about migrations if it is no longer exact.

Files likely touched: src/lib/db/** (new), src/lib/tasks/types.ts (new), scripts/check-rules.test.ts (new), docs/current/how/persistence.md (new), docs/current/data-model.md (new), docs/current/_overview.md, docs/current/README.md, docs/current/setup.md.
Do not add npm dependencies. Do not create repository or validation code (sibling ticks own src/lib/tasks/repository.ts and validate.ts).
